spine.deviation_notes: APPROX: The identity IS the kill-to-spawn shadowling swarm. Engine maps the player projectile loop + on-kill trigger for spawn consequence, but the dynamic swarm-size-as-DPS mechanic (shadowlings are the primary damage delivery at high kill-chain) is not natively representable. Source player would recognize the skeleton but miss the swarm-scaling experience. Not GAPPED because the player's own ranged attack loop remains the trigger mechanic.

skills.delivery_notes: Cursed projectile ranged attack. 'shadow magic that has a chance of converting slain enemies into Shadowling bats' — shadow here describes the curse mechanism, not a damage type. No shadow damage-type descriptor attested. On kill → shadowling spawn (trigger consequence). Element-silent.
'call forth a terrifying Shadowling Brute at the target location' — placed-proxy at target. Totem geometry per totem-vs-companion law (placed at location, not following companion).
Passive: Shadowling allies last longer and deal more damage. Scaling passive — self_buff / traits lane.

mapping_json.motion_frame: Shoot Shadowling Ammo-cursed projectiles to kill enemies; on-kill converts enemies into Shadowling bats (10s swarm); Shadowling Brute as direct placed summon; maintain kill-chain to sustain swarm.

resource_economy.charge_note: Charge built from attacks; full bar grants passive bonuses

mapping_json.fidelity_notes: Element: 'shadow magic' is mechanism-flavor, not damage-type descriptor — element-silent per D4 NAME-ONLY LAW (shadow used adjectivally to describe the curse, not as 'deals shadow damage'). Kit is pet-rider (player shoots to generate kills; shadowlings supplement) not pure pet-core — player damage loop exists. APPROX-grade because shadowling swarm is a significant identity dimension the engine cannot fully represent; the on-kill spawn trigger is approximated via trigger_grammar. Near-miss §0: wanted shadow element — 'shadow magic' is the closest text but fails damage-type-descriptor test.
